title: Tuesday's boring SaaS, 20 October 2026
dek: Tuesday, 20 October 2026. Ten are Stripe-verified, including a newer Conductor number. The Caribbean fleet note is self-reported, and there is no company name.

companies.name: Snap2Pass
companies.description: Upload a selfie and it gets resized, background-fixed and checked against your country's exact document spec. It covers passport, visa and ID photos (founder-stated). Homepage: "500K+ photos processed", "166 countries supported", "99.8% acceptance rate", "ICAO 9303 compliant", "14-day money-back guarantee", free reshoots if rejected. It also offers same-day printing at Walgreens/CVS (~$0.39) or mailed prints ($7.47) (company-stated). There's a B2B tier for travel agencies and photo studios: a branded client photo link or upload at the counter, plus an API. Pricing: $20 for 4 clients, volume packs down to $2 a client, no subscription (company-stated). The app lists in-app purchases "starting at $4.99" (company-stated). ~20,000 estimated users (founder-stated). Founded Jan 2023, US, founder "oalpay". There's an AI headshot upsell too, but the core job is a government form requirement.
companies.evidence: MRR $0 (one-off purchases) · 0 subscriptions Last 30 days $6,131 (-8.9%) · last 3 months $18,978 · last 6 months $33,624 Last 12 months $74,924 · all-time $191,674 · last 7 days $1,224 Monthly: $5,004 (Nov 2025) → $7,735 (Jan) → $8,176 (Mar) → $4,743 (May) → $5,291 (Jul) → $6,066 (Aug) → $7,321 (Sep); Oct MTD $3,775. Steady $4.7–8.2k band, no cliff. Revenue synced 20 October 2026 ~06:37 Warsaw.
companies.indieAngle: Do the EU/PL version. Polish passport and ID photos (zdjęcie do dowodu/paszportu) have a strict spec, and so do Schengen/US/UK/Chinese visa photos for Poles and Ukrainians in Poland. Sell to consumers at ~20 zł, and give fotograf studios and visa agencies a white-label link on credits.
companies.whyItPrints: Consulates and passport offices reject bad photos, so people pay a few dollars to not get rejected. Demand comes from passport renewals, visa season and Google searches for "<country> visa photo size". The B2B side (agencies, studios) turns one-off buyers into repeat accounts.

companies.name: Trackly → Changeflow

Target persona: "compliance officers, regulatory teams, strategy & market intelligence teams, PR teams" (founder-stated). One case on the page: a healthcare compliance team cut Federal Register review "from 10 hours/week to 30 minutes" (company-stated). companies.indieAngle: Regulatory-change watch for one Polish vertical: Dziennik Ustaw / KNF / UODO / URE / NFZ notices for accounting offices, pharmacies, energy traders or fintechs. Charge 99–499 zł/mo per firm, with the first customers coming from biura rachunkowe (accounting offices) that need to track rule changes for clients.
companies.whyItPrints: Someone in every regulated company has to read regulator websites, competitor pricing pages and policy notices every week. This replaces that reading with an alert. B2B, sold per seat or plan, and it has been running for 8 years. The profile describes it as "B2B SaaS charged through Recurly", so the Stripe figures may not show everything (my read).

companies.name: LemmiLink
companies.description: A marketplace that connects advertisers with publishers. You browse 175,000+ websites filtered by topic, metrics and price, then buy guest posts, homepage links or links inserted into pages that already rank. Writing and indexing are included, with an "indexed or replaced" guarantee. There are also express link packs, forum links, done-for-you SEO, a public API and an MCP server (founder-stated). Pricing: from €5 per link, pay-as-you-go wallet, packs and monthly plans (founder-stated). ~2,700 estimated users (founder-stated). Homepage: "Des liens sur 175 000 sites vérifiés", "Utilisé par +70 agences SEO et 3 200 entreprises", and an unpublished order is refunded to your wallet (company-stated). Founded Oct 2023, France, founder Sofiane.
companies.evidence: MRR $225 · 1 active subscription (pay-per-link marketplace) Last 30 days $4,213 (-49.8%) · last 3 months $18,204 · last 6 months $34,510 Last 12 months $84,612 · all-time $134,128 · last 24 h $662 Monthly: $8,953 (Nov 2025) → $9,527 (Dec) → $9,770 (Feb) → $8,642 (Mar) → ~$5.2–6.2k (Apr–Aug) → $7,587 (Sep); Oct MTD $2,480. Down from ~$9k winter months to ~$6k, so softening. Revenue synced 20 October 2026 ~08:56 Warsaw.
companies.indieAngle: Poland has the same SEO market, with link sellers like WhitePress and the old SEO-marketplace crowd. A smaller wedge works: a vetted marketplace for one vertical, such as legal/finance/medical Polish publishers, with an indexing guarantee. Or sell the publisher side as SaaS: a "list your site, get orders" inventory tool for Polish bloggers.
companies.whyItPrints: Link-building is the dullest SEO chore, and agencies buy links every month. A marketplace takes a cut on every order and holds the prepaid wallet. MRR is tiny because almost everything is per-order.

companies.name: Quantt

Every lesson is code you write and tests you pass, e.g. a momentum backtest with a kill-switch on drawdown (company-stated). Meta description: "60+ interactive courses" covering Python for finance, derivatives pricing, portfolio theory, risk management (company-stated). Pricing: £39.95/month, £249.95/year, enterprise custom, 30-day money-back (founder-stated). Target: CS grads, career changers, juniors breaking into quant (founder-stated). Founded Dec 2025, UK. 154 active subscriptions.

companies.indieAngle: "Learn by passing tests" for another paid career gate: Excel/VBA for Big 4 audit juniors, SQL for analysts, actuarial exam prep, or Polish CFA/ACCA candidates. Use auto-graded exercises in the browser and an annual plan priced for students.
companies.whyItPrints: Like Dataford (19 Oct) and Writing9 (18 Oct): an evergreen career gate, with high-income buyers who pay £40/month without blinking. Interactive coding with auto-graded tests is hard to copy with a YouTube playlist. It went from zero to ~$6k MRR in ten months.

companies.name: Apogee

Profile founded Feb 2026 (revenue starts at ~$3.2k in Feb, so the business probably existed before; not stated). France, founder Mathieu (832 X followers). 43 subscriptions; L30 margin 80%.

companies.indieAngle: Same "bulk ops over a hated ad UI" play, but for Allegro Ads, Google Merchant Center feeds, or LinkedIn Campaign Manager. Make the first version Polish-language for local performance agencies, then add an agency seat price.
companies.whyItPrints: It's ops glue for a UI everybody hates (Ads Manager). Agencies launching dozens of creatives a week for many clients are the buyers. It's French-language, which keeps US competitors out, and revenue has been flat-steady ~$3k/month for eight months.

companies.name: TextWork
companies.description: Candidates text to apply, and an agent screens them over SMS, asks your qualifying questions, schedules interviews and hands recruiters a clean summary. It works after hours and over weekends (founder-stated). It plugs into SmartRecruiters or your ATS (company-stated). Target: "teams that hire at volume and cannot call every applicant: hourly and frontline roles, skilled trades, staffing desks" (founder-stated). Pricing: Starter $99/mo, Growth $199/mo, Enterprise (homepage). Homepage counters (rendered 20 Oct): "202+ jobsites", "277,459+ text messages exchanged", "11,693+ applicants screened" (company-stated). ~8,000 estimated users (founder-stated). Founded Jan 2018, US, founder Brian (1.6k X followers).

companies.indieAngle: Polish blue-collar and Ukrainian-worker hiring runs on phone calls and WhatsApp. Build "aplikuj SMS-em/WhatsAppem" pre-screening (availability, permits, driving licence, start date) for agencje pracy tymczasowej (temp agencies) and logistics warehouses, priced per site.
companies.whyItPrints: Staffing desks and field-service companies lose applicants who wait days for a call back. SMS screening is plumbing between job boards, the ATS and a recruiter's calendar. Only 2 active subscriptions, so this is a couple of enterprise contracts (my read of the numbers), very concentrated.

companies.name: Anonymous Caribbean fleet-tracking company
companies.description: The founder has run a fleet-tracking company for ~12 years, selling GPS tracking and AI dashcams to commercial fleets across the Caribbean, with a smaller operation in Colombia (founder-stated).
companies.evidence: ~370 clients, roughly $1.6M ARR, "on track for about 30% growth in the Caribbean this year" (founder-stated) Revenue per client ≈ $4.3k/year (my arithmetic from the two stated numbers) Not verified; no company name or website given.

sources.label: Reddit r/Entrepreneur post by u/imjp (5 Oct 2026, ~20:09 Warsaw)

companies.indieAngle: Two ways in. (1) Fleet telematics for an underserved region where you speak the language and know the buyers, e.g. Polish/Ukrainian transport SMEs with 5–50 trucks, bundling the tachograph/e-TOLL/SENT paperwork. (2) Build the dunning glue he lacks: wire-transfer reconciliation + auto-suspend + late-fee invoicing for B2B hardware-subscription companies in multi-country markets.
companies.whyItPrints: Hardware + monthly SaaS sold to trucking, logistics and government fleets in small island markets that big US/EU players ignore. Billing runs across 20+ territories by wire transfer. The founder's own problem is the boring part: "almost half our clients, about 170 of 370, pay late", and "some of our gov clients are pretty much always 90+ days late". The fix he's planning is automatic account disconnects, annual billing for bad payers and late fees (founder-stated, in comments).
